item.title: Schedule: Texas Route 66 Festival returns to Amarillo June 4-13, 2026
item.description: The Texas Panhandle is set to celebrate one of America’s most iconic highways this summer with the return of the Texas Route 66 Festival, running June 4 through June 13, 2026.

item.title: Yellow City Rundown Feb. 2-6: Adams sentencing, Bird Flu, Booker ISD
item.description: On this episode of the Yellow City Rundown for the week of Feb. 2-6, we focus on the sentencing of Tifany Adams, Amarillo Public Health and Amarillo Animal Management and Welfare are responding to reports of sick and dead birds in the Amarillo area, and how Booker ISD is helping families after the fire at the Preferred Beef Plant.

item.title: 1 seriously injured in wreck near I-40 and Paramount Friday
item.description: Multiple crews are on the scene of a wreck near I-40 and Paramount Friday evening.

item.title: Eastbound lanes blocked after wreck on I-40 Friday
item.description: AMARILLO, Texas (KAMR/KCIT) — The Amarillo Police Department is currently on the scene of a wreck that resulted in lane closures on I-40 East near the interchange Friday evening. Officials said that all eastbound lanes are blocked.

item.title: Man in Potter County sentenced to life in prison on child sexual assault charges
item.description: The 47th District Attorney's Office announced that a man in Potter County was sentenced to two life sentences on charges of aggravated sexual assault of a child.

item.title: Woman in Randall County pleads guilty in 2023 homicide case
item.description: A woman who was arrested in connection with a November 2023 homicide pleaded guilty and was sentenced Thursday.

item.title: Man sentenced to 50 years for a deadly wreck in 2024
item.description: The 47th District Attorney’s Office announced that a 19-year-old man was sentenced to two decades in prison for a drunk driving wreck that happened in 2024 that killed two teenagers and seriously injured another.

item.title: What the future holds for the Panhandle-Plains Historical Museum
item.description: The Panhandle-Plains Historical Museum has remained closed since the a fire marshal report cited safety violations. WT President Walter Wendler decided to close the museum in March, citing danger to the public.
